title: Live stream is a second binding of the whole client-provider draft, to find its gaps
description:
Epic mimid-e64f; docs/design/binary-live-stream.md §1, §9 questions 1 and 6.

Context: the first version of the note proposed the CBOR live stream as a transport that only replaces polling, and recommended waiting.

Chosen (Mark, 2026-11-20): build the stream now, as a second binding of the same client-provider operations as draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00. Its purpose is to find gaps in that draft by restating every operation without JMAP's conventions. It is not a transport upgrade.

- Scope is the whole draft: sending and the hub's answer, KeyPackage publish and claim, room create/update/membership, consent, assets/blobs, catch-up/history, and every other method the agent uses or a client would need. The "later" items of the first note move into version 1.
- JMAP stays the standard and the agent's default; the stream sits behind a configuration switch on agent and server.
- Integration tests run the same scenarios over both bindings side by side, and the results must agree.
- Main output: docs/design/binary-live-stream-findings.md, one entry per gap (what, where in the draft with a quote, JMAP binding, stream, proposed text preferring MAY over SHOULD over MUST).
- No edits to jmap-chat-spec: proposed text lives only in the findings log.
- Not an Internet-Draft now (§9 question 6): mimid's own protocol until a second implementation wants it.
